new_statements.translation: The Congolese languages of group C20 have two types of tones: 1) level tones: a) the high tone (´), b) the low tone (unmarked). In all these languages the two tones carry the distinctive function. 2) contour tones: a) the rising contour tone, b) the falling contour tone. They affect long vowels, which we transcribe with two vowels. All these languages realise combinations of tones of both types.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Akwa, like the other six Congolese C20 languages surveyed (Mboko, Ngare, Koyo, Mbosi, Likwala, Likuba), is described as a two-tone language (H vs. unmarked L, lexically distinctive; rising/falling contours on long vowels). The accessible pages say nothing about word stress or accent; no stress statement was found in any opened source.
new_statements.exceptions: none regarding prosody; the statement is a group-level synthesis ('dans toutes ces langues') explicitly covering Akwa (akwá), whose language-specific phonology section (pp. 38-277) is outside the preview.
new_statements.domain_note: Lexical tone on the word/morpheme; examples are citation forms of nouns and infinitives (p.275: bas+bas nganga, haut+bas, bas+haut ngubé, haut+haut). Statement is typological, made by the fieldworker himself for all seven languages including Akwa, so first-hand but not Akwa-specific in wording.
new_statements.identity_note: Ndinga Oba 2003 treats 'akwá' (Guthrie C22, district of Makoua, Cuvette; ~25,000 speakers; varieties: Makoua, axe Etoumbi, axe Owando, Akwa-Opa) as one of seven C20 languages; the quoted tone statement is a group-level synthesis explicitly including Akwa, not an Akwa-only sentence. The Moscow grammar (Aksenova & Toporova 2002) and Toporova 2009 describe the Akwa-Mbangi dialect ('диалект аква-мбанги') of the Makoua area from speaker E.A. Ossete — same glottocode akwa1248. Apondza 2003 describes Ndongo-Nyama, listed by Ndinga Oba as an Akwa-speaking 'terre' in Makoua district (no separate glottocode known).

sources.note: Section II 'Typologie', p.279 'Les tons': the Congolese C20 languages (Mboko, Akwa, Ngare, Koyo, Mbosi, Likwala, Likuba) have two level tones, high (marked) and low (unmarked), and 'dans toutes ces langues, les deux tons assument la fonction distinctive'; plus rising/falling contour tones on long vowels; p.275 tone combinations. No mention of stress/accent anywhere in the accessible pages (front matter, introduction, Akwa presentation pp.25-26, typology pp.279-289). The Akwa-specific phonology study (ch. II section I, somewhere in pp.38-277) is not in the preview.
Only one datapoint (73A optative, citing Aksenova & Toporova 2002); no stress features (14A-17A) coded for Akwa.
